extraction.document_summary: AIA Enhanced Cancer Protect is a cancer protection plan that provides payouts from the first cancer diagnosis through up to two major stage cancer relapses. The brochure states coverage of up to S$700,000, with each relapse claimable two years apart, and premiums that do not change yearly “1” (premiums are set by entry age and may be adjusted later). Buyers can choose a coverage period of 20 years or “till 65 years old”. The core mechanics are: (1) first diagnosis payout at 100% of the coverage amount, (2) 1st and 2nd major-stage relapse payouts at 100% each, and (3) optional Enhanced Cancer Protect Plus add-on that increases total coverage up to 400%, adds early-stage (50% payout) and catastrophic cancer coverage, and shows an example where catastrophic cancer triggers an additional payout while the 2nd relapse benefit also pays.
quality_notes: Document provides clear benefit mechanics for first diagnosis, two relapse claims (two years apart), and optional add-on early/catastrophic coverage via worked examples and diagrams.
Exact definitions of covered “Major Cancer”, “Intermediate/Stage”, and “catastrophic cancer” are not enumerated in detail; only a list of early-stage cancers is provided.
No explicit sum-assured range table or entry/maximum ages are stated beyond coverage ending at age 65 or after 20 years.
Underwriting type, medical exam requirement, grace period, and free-look period are not stated.

aliases: AIA Enhanced Cancer Protect (Thrice the Assurance With One Cancer Plan)
policies.quick_summary: Cancer protection plan covering first diagnosis and up to two major-stage relapses, with relapse claims spaced two years apart. Coverage can be for 20 years or till age 65. Optional Enhanced Cancer Protect Plus add-on expands coverage to include early-stage and catastrophic cancer (up to 400% total coverage). Premiums are determined at entry age; yearly premium changes may occur based on claims experience/regulatory changes per notes (not guaranteed). Once catastrophic/termination events occur, the brochure’s examples show termination of relevant benefits and continued premium payments to maintain relapse/catastrophic coverage.
coverage_scope: First diagnosis of major cancer (major stage) with 100% of coverage amount
Up to two major stage cancer relapses (Relapse 1 and Relapse 2) claimable two years apart
Optional add-on (Enhanced Cancer Protect Plus) includes early-stage, intermediate-stage, and catastrophic cancer coverage and increases total coverage up to 400%
policies.coverage_term_description: Choose between a coverage period of 20 years, or till 65 years old.
policy_termination_events: The brochure’s examples state that after catastrophic cancer diagnosis, the policy and add-on cover will terminate (as described in the example).

The brochure’s examples also show that certain benefits terminate after an early-stage or major-stage diagnosis event (e.g., “major stage cancer benefit terminates” and “cancer relapse benefit terminates” in the example).
important_caveats: Cancer relapse benefit is payable only if the diagnosed Major Cancer condition meets the definitions and waiting period as stated in the policy contract.
Waiting period and survival period are applicable before the benefits will be payable.
Premiums are not guaranteed and may be adjusted based on future claims experience/regulatory requirements (per terms).
Value-added services are not contractual benefits and can be cancelled/terminated by partners/AIA without notice.

review_notes: Policy is treated as cancer-only critical illness protection based on brochure wording and stated benefit events (major cancer diagnosis/relapse and add-on early/catastrophic cancer).
No explicit underwriting/exclusion details were extracted because the document only provides generic “exclusions such as pre-existing conditions” language without naming specific exclusions.

Catastrophic cancer amount is taken as equal to the coverage amount in the provided example; the brochure does not state a general percentage for catastrophic payout beyond the diagram and example sequencing.
